images.scene: ULTRA-WIDE fisheye-like lens, camera lying on the packed dirt ground only a few steps from the open door of a small rustic wooden chapel, looking steeply up (extreme contre-plongee): the chapel front looms tall and close, its rough plank facade filling the middle of the frame, and right above the doorway a large old bronze bell hangs from a weathered wooden beam, rope pulled taut, caught mid-swing. Working people in simple clothes and hats stream past the camera into the door on BOTH sides, their legs and backs large and close at the left and right edges, dust on their shoes, filling the frame edge to edge. The chapel is humble, built by a small town with its own hands. The top of the chapel and the sky dissolve upward into bright overexposed haze.

A meeting table right after a pointless meeting, no people: crumpled plastic cups, a cold half-full coffee pot, a cup tipped over with a coffee stain, crumpled napkins, a pen left uncapped, chairs pushed back at odd angles, seen from close at table height. Hard side light from a window. Pale bare wall above fills the top fifth.

A heavy old mechanical stopwatch lying on top of a closed notebook on a long wooden desk, a pen beside it, seen from very close and low so the stopwatch is HUGE, its top edge reaching the middle of the frame, morning light raking from the side. The surface the objects rest on extends away from the camera and fades softly into bright haze; there is NO wall behind it and NO visible table edge.

Inside a small Brazilian company: the owner, a man in his fifties in a plain button-up shirt, standing at a whiteboard tapping a hand-drawn bar chart of simple blocks, while three employees in matching company polo shirts sit at a meeting table with open notebooks looking at the board; a plain wall clock on the wall beside the board. The owner is large in the frame, upper body and head fully visible. The whiteboard has no frame and its upper part is washed out by strong window light so it merges with the bright haze above; the wall dissolves upward into light with no painted band and no horizontal line. Any marks on the board are tiny scribbles, completely ILLEGIBLE. CINEMATIC DIRECTION: camera at chest height, one strong directional light source raking across the scene, deep shadows, dramatic contrast. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist.

A tear-off daily desk calendar on a wooden desk with a huge heap of its torn-off pages piled beside it, hundreds of small torn sheets spilling across the desk, seen from close and slightly above, hard side light. Any printed or handwritten marks are tiny scribbles, completely ILLEGIBLE, reduced to grey smudged lines; the photograph itself stays sharp. Pale wall above fills the top fifth.

Inside the cab of an old pickup truck on a dirt road: the driver's two hands gripping the big thin steering wheel, seen from just behind his shoulder, the dusty road ahead through the windshield bending to the left, and far ahead the small wooden chapel with its bell tower at the end of the road. The wheel and hands are large in the frame; the sky through the windshield dissolves into bright haze. Same world as the opening scene: a small Brazilian rural town, packed dirt roads, rough wooden buildings, working people in simple clothes and hats, dust in the light.
